title: Can you solve it? 🔑 Who knew the secret? (Colour) #shorts
description:
The village hall in Tidewhistle Cove has a spare key, hidden under the big terracotta plant pot by the front door. It hangs on a short blue ribbon so it's easy to find in the dark, and only the hall committee knows about it. 🔑

On Saturday night, the raffle hamper (jams, chutneys and a whole Cornish cheese) vanished from the locked hall. No broken window, no forced door: whoever took it let themselves in with a key and locked up again.

On Sunday, Constable Ollie lifted the pot, looked underneath and set it down. All he said was that the spare key was still there. Then he and Agnes spoke to three helpers:

Demelza Rowe left at five and went straight to her sister's for supper (her sister confirms it).
Pip Carew went home at six and had no idea there was a spare key at all.
Mr Spargo, who built the tombola stall: "A spare key? Under a plant pot? I had no idea. And I'm sure I'd remember a key on a blue ribbon like that."

Ollie and Agnes looked at each other.

description:

Wenna Polglaze shares her antique shop with Admiral, an elderly grey parrot. He picks up any phrase he hears a few times in a row and repeats it for days. He knows "Good morning", "Pieces of eight" and Wenna's favourite, "Put the kettle on".

On Thursday afternoon Wenna popped out for half an hour, leaving the shop locked and Admiral on his perch. Three people have keys: Tamsin Trevelyan, Mr Fenwick, and Mr Pascoe, who cleans the inside windows once a month.

When Wenna came back, her antique silver thimble was gone, and Admiral was squawking something he had never said before: "Mind how you go, my lovely!"

Tamsin says she was in her own shop all afternoon, Mr Fenwick says he was at the grocer's, and all three say they weren't in Wenna's shop that day.

title: Can you solve it? ⭐ Whose story doesn't fit? (Colour) #shorts
description:
The Tidewhistle Cove Gazette comes out every Friday, and Agnes reads it cover to cover over breakfast. This week the back page had a notice from the stargazing club: "New moon this Saturday. The darkest night of the month. Perfect for spotting meteors. Bring a blanket and a flask." ⭐

On Saturday evening the club met on the clifftop with their telescopes and a special guest: Miss Clemo, an astronomer from the city staying at the inn. They had borrowed a beautiful antique star chart from the museum, spread out on a little table in the club's tent. At eleven everyone went outside to look at the sky. At midnight, the star chart was gone.

Three people had left the clifftop early:

Demelza Rowe left at half past ten. Captain Quill walked her home, and they were both at her cottage before eleven.
Miss Clemo left at about a quarter past eleven, saying she was tired: "I walked back to the inn along the cliff path. It was such a lovely night. The moon was full and bright, so bright I could see every pebble without a torch. I never went back into the tent."

Agnes thought of the little notice on the back page of the Gazette.

title: Can you solve it? 🔔 Who could reach the bell? (Colour) #shorts
description:
Above the door of the sailing club hangs a brass ship's bell, rung for the start of every race. Its hook is so high that even the tallest person in the village has to stretch up on tiptoe to reach it. The tallest person in the village is Tobias Ferris of the lifeboat crew: six and a half feet tall. 🔔

The club's stepladder lives in a locked cupboard, and Agnes, the club treasurer, keeps the only key on her own key ring. On Sunday the cupboard was still locked with the ladder inside, and the only other thing in the porch to stand on was a tiny stool that has been broken for months. And the bell was gone from its hook.

Three people were at the club's quiz night on Saturday:

Loveday Nance, a little over five feet tall: at the quiz table all evening; she couldn't reach that hook standing on a chair.
Mr Fenwick, not much taller than Loveday: left early with a headache.
Tobias: at the quiz too, home at ten. "I didn't touch the bell. I hardly ever even notice it."

Agnes jingled her key ring and looked up at the empty hook.

description:

Demelza Rowe, lemon sorbet: tapped her card.
Pip, double mint: paid with a banknote and got his change from the till.
Mr Nankervis, staying at the inn, vanilla cone: counted out a handful of coins from his pocket, straight into the till, unchecked.
